newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: French tighten controls on Swiss beef imports.
newsitem.headline: French tighten controls on Swiss beef imports.

text.p: France has slapped restrictions on cattle imports from Switzerland which has the highest incidence of "mad cow" disease after Britain, the Swiss Economics Ministry said on Wednesday.
The French measures that came into effect on November 1 require that imported animals come from herds known to be free of the disease Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE).
They also bar cattle born before December 1, 1990, when Switzerland imposed rules aimed at stopping the spread of BSE.
Berne's Federal Veterinary Office last week said Swiss law already required export cattle to meet these two standards.
BSE or mad cow disease is a brain-wasting affliction that scientists say may cause a human equivalent, Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease.

Germany and Austria have barred imports of Swiss beef due to human health fears over BSE. Italy recently lifted a ban but requires cattle to come from BSE-free herds and to be clearly marked as Swiss.
Switzerland has reported 226 BSE cases from 1990 through October despite new rules in December 1990 that forbid feeding cattle beef bone and remains that could help spread the disease.
The Swiss cabinet in September proposed the slaughter of up to 230,000 cattle in a bid to stamp out mad cow disease in Switzerland and restore consumer confidence.
